missionPremise: Dispatch _dispatches/2026-09-02_factory-reaper-phantoms_dispatch.md, itself sourced from the FACTORY-JOB-SIGTERM close's own leave_behind: reapStartedRuns() matches only status='started', but 8 of ~24 job files write status='running' to startRun, so their runs were structurally invisible to every reap tick, forever, regardless of age -- a starved mechanism (correct downstream logic, never-supplied precondition for that class).
completionPredicate: The reap tick's own SELECT, syncRunStatusFromTermination, and parentState all check membership in IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES (['started','running']) rather than a bare 'started' string; a genuine falsifier proves the status string itself is what changed; the fix is merged and deployed to 10 job resources (14 counting the SIGTERM close's own 4); both phantom rows named in the dispatch are reconciled via the fixed mechanism itself (recorder='reaper', not a manual override); and a live zero-stale-rows query, run after both the reap tick and the redeploy sweep, returns no rows -- the exact evidence the dispatch asked for.
scopeBasis: Redeployed the 3 additional cloudbuild pipelines this repo has checked in beyond the SIGTERM close's own 2 (conformant.yaml, p2-juris.yaml, publish.yaml), covering 10 more job resources at zero configuration risk since each pipeline already fully specifies its own jobs' secrets/env/memory. 12 remaining job resources have no discoverable pipeline in this repo; reconstructing their gcloud run jobs deploy commands from scratch was judged out of proportion risk (a deploy REPLACES the spec; a dropped --set-secrets or --memory flag would be a silent regression this session has no way to catch), so they are named explicitly as deploy-on-next-natural-touch rather than swept. factory-atoms-cad runs a distinct image entirely and does not contain this code -- correctly out of scope, not a gap.

open: 12 hauska-factory-image job resources (factory-bake-migrate, factory-cc-publish, factory-console-audit, factory-landing-cad, factory-landing-footprint, factory-landing-import, factory-landing-parcel, factory-landing-pipeline, factory-landing-wells, factory-manifest-import, factory-missing-env, factory-snapshot) carry both fixes in source but run stale images until their own next deploy -- a run started by one of these between now and that deploy would still leave a phantom row on an external kill (the SIGTERM guard) and would still be invisible to the reap tick if it happens to write status='running' (the reaper fix). Low practical risk: none of these are named in this session's active work, and IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES already covers 'running' the moment any of them does redeploy.
The redeploy-sweep gap itself (no checked-in pipeline for those 12 jobs) is a standing operational gap worth its own card if a future incident traces to one of them running stale for a long period.
